citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
A bottle of pyrantel expired on 6/26/25. The licensee stated he has probably used it recently. Expired
medications/products doesn't ensure that the product given to the animal is safe and of a high quality. The expired
medication/product could be ineffective or toxic to the animal(s). Expired medications and products must not be used on
regulated animals and need to be removed from the storage area that is reserved for use in regulated animals. Correct
starting on 6/18/26.

Two litters of puppies (one litter had 6 puppies and the other litter had 3 puppies) did not have health certificates
completed by a licensed veterinarian prior to being shipped. Shipping dogs without having a completed health certificate
doesn't ensure the dogs being shipped are in good health. All dogs being shipped must have a health certificate
completed by a licensed veterinarian no more than 10 days prior to the delivery of the dogs. Correct starting on 6/18/26.

Six puppies born on 2/20/26 were sold and transported on 4/16/26. The puppies would have been 55 days old on the day
of sale which is one day shy of the required 8 weeks of age that they are required to be before being sold and
transported. Dogs younger than 8 weeks of age are more susceptible to stresses that occur from travelling and being
placed into a new facility. Their immune systems are more susceptible to becoming comprised which could cause them to
become sick and even die. The licensee must not sell any puppies under 8 weeks of age unless it is directly to the end
consumer. Correct starting on 6/18/26.

Two areas of the kennel were in disrepair. One enclosure had a hole in the see through doggy door with jagged
(unsmooth edges). Another enclosure had the wire front of the enclosure loose and coming out (bowing) into the walkway
as the dogs jumped on it.
A hole in an enclosure door with jagged edges could cause injury to the dogs in that enclosure. It could also allow pests
such as flies to enter the building. The wire front of the other enclosure coming loose and bowing outward as the dogs
jump on it could result in a dog getting stuck or injured when the wire front bows outward and creates an opening into the
walkway. It could also result in the dog escaping the enclosure.
Housing facilities for all dogs must be designed and constructed so they are structurally sound. They must be kept in good
repair and must protect the dogs from injury and contain the animals securely.
Correct by 7/18/26.

Multiple outdoor enclosures had rust on the fencing and posts. Rust does not allow for the enclosure to be readily cleaned
and sanitized. All enclosures must be constructed and maintained so they are free of rust and can be readily cleaned and
sanitized. Correct by 7/18/26.

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
The enclosures appeared to be dirty during inspection. Fecal matter/dirt was smeared on the walls of the enclosures,
around the frames of the openings (that lead to the outdoor part of the enclosure), on the doggy doors, and on the black
mats that the dogs lay/sit on. The licensee stated that he sanitizes about once a month and last sanitized the enclosures
about 2-3 weeks ago. Not sanitizing the enclosures on a biweekly basis (or more often if necessary) allows for fecal
material and grime to build up which can contribute to the spread of disease. The licensee must sanitize the enclosures
every two weeks or more often as necessary to prevent the accumulation of dirt, debris, excreta, and other disease
hazards. Correct by 7/2/26.

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
The exercise area that adult dogs use has overgrown weeds and grass. Overgrown weeds and grass make the area
difficult to observe dogs in it (to be sure they are secure), is difficult to clean, and can create areas for rodents and pests
to live in. Ensure that vegetation in the exercise area is controlled in a manner that allows cleaning of the area and to
protect the health and well-being of the dogs that use that area.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
End of report.
